designSequence.waveName: Dependency, Packaging, and Public API Architecture

purpose: Define the initial Python distribution model, build backend, project metadata, optional Prefect installation extra, dependency lock strategy, package discovery, and clean installation/build verification profiles for GPWCF.

included: PEP 517/518 build-system and PEP 621 project metadata.
Setuptools build backend selection and pin.
Core runtime dependency metadata and optional Prefect extra.
Source package discovery and package-data policy.
Installation commands and packaging verification profiles.
Future conditions for splitting Core and Prefect Integration distributions.
excluded: Actual creation of pyproject.toml or lock files.
Actual installation/upgrading of Setuptools, Prefect, or other packages.
Implementation of production Core or Prefect Integration source modules.
Reopening the accepted Prefect 3.9.2 integration decision.
A GPWCF-local dependency bundle or copied virtual environment.

architecturalOptions.name: TwoSeparateDistributionsImmediately
architecturalOptions.description: Build gpwcf-core and gpwcf-prefect as separately published distributions from the initial release.
advantages: Physical installation isolation: Core consumers do not receive Prefect Integration source files.
Independent versioning and release cadence are possible.
Integration can evolve its dependency closure separately.
disadvantages: Requires coordinated multi-distribution build/release and version compatibility policy from the first release.
Adds package metadata/build configuration and release automation complexity before multiple integrations or independent release cadence are demonstrated.
May create premature distribution boundaries while Core and its initial Prefect Integration are developed as one framework release.

architecturalOptions.name: SingleDistributionWithOptionalPrefectExtra
architecturalOptions.description: Build one gpwcf distribution containing Core and the optional Prefect Integration package. Declare Prefect only under the optional [prefect] extra; Core base metadata has no third-party runtime dependencies.
advantages: One versioned framework artifact and simpler initial release process.
Core-only installation does not install Prefect.
Prefect Integration remains a separate logical package and Public API surface.
The existing monorepo/package structure can evolve without immediate multi-distribution release machinery.
A future split remains possible without changing Core domain ownership.
disadvantages: Core-only consumers receive the Integration source package files even though they do not install Prefect.
Integration and Core initially share one distribution version/release cadence.
Import guards and packaging tests are required to ensure the optional boundary is real.

architecturalOptions.name: SingleDistributionWithPrefectAsBaseDependency
architecturalOptions.description: Install Prefect as a mandatory base dependency of GPWCF.
advantages: Simplifies integration imports for every consumer.
disadvantages: Makes Core dependent on an external workflow runtime.
Forces Prefect onto consumers that do not select Prefect Integration.

selectedDesign.decision: Use one gpwcf distribution for the initial release with a rigorously optional Prefect extra. Preserve the logical Core and Prefect Integration package/API boundaries, and split distributions only when independent release/dependency needs are demonstrated.

distribution.name: gpwcf
distribution.versioning: Semantic Versioning for the distribution's supported Public API. Internal implementation changes that do not alter supported contracts do not require a major API break.
distribution.releaseCadence: One framework release initially; Core and Prefect Integration public contracts are versioned together while the optional extra controls runtime dependency installation.
futureSplitTrigger: Prefect Integration requires a materially different release cadence from Core.
Additional workflow integrations create independent dependency closures or platform support matrices.
Integration implementation size/distribution policy requires consumers not to receive its source package files.
A consumer demand for independent Integration versioning is demonstrated.
distribution.futureSplitRule: If split is justified, preserve the public import namespace and define explicit Core/Integration version compatibility; do not introduce the split merely to simulate dependency isolation already provided by the optional extra.

buildSystem.classification: Isolated build-system dependency only; it is not a GPWCF runtime dependency.
whySetuptools: It is a stable, widely used Python packaging backend with PEP 517 build hooks.
It supports declarative PEP 621 project metadata in pyproject.toml.
The current 84.2.1 release declares Python >=3.10 support and includes Python 3.15 build support in its release history.
The project uses a pure-Python src layout and does not require a custom backend.
buildSystem.whyNotCustomBackend: No custom build logic or native extension build is required. A custom backend would introduce unnecessary code and maintenance.
buildSystem.wheelDependency: Do not add wheel as a separate build-system requirement unless a clean build demonstrates a concrete need; setuptools.build_meta provides the wheel/sdist build hooks.

buildFrontend.classification: Developer/build frontend only; not a package runtime dependency.
buildFrontend.versionPolicy: Pin in the separate development/build lock after the build toolchain is selected.

buildSystem.buildIsolation: Use PEP 517 build isolation. The build frontend creates an isolated environment containing only the declared build-system requirements; do not rely on packages incidentally installed in SMRB .env.

projectMetadata.pythonSupportPolicy: The current evidenced support baseline is CPython 3.15.1 x64 on Windows x64. The initial requires-python range is limited to Python 3.15.x; broader versions/platforms require an explicit CI/test support matrix before metadata is widened.
projectMetadata.metadataCaution: Author, license expression, classifiers, project URLs, and description must be populated from approved repository/project metadata during implementation; do not invent legal or ownership information in this design.

prefectExtra.meaning: Install the accepted external workflow runtime only when the consumer opts into Prefect Integration.

runtimeDependencies.otherOptionalPatternExtras: Do not create empty extras for Validation, Error Handling, Observation, or Diagnostics while their generic contracts have no third-party runtime dependencies. Add a pattern-specific extra only if that pattern later acquires an actual runtime package requirement.
runtimeDependencies.noBasePrefect: Prefect must not appear in [project].dependencies or any unconditional Core requirement file.
runtimeDependencies.noGeneratorDependency: pygccxml>=3.0.0 remains in the Generator consumer requirements only.

packageDiscovery.discovery: Setuptools package discovery is rooted at src and includes gpwcf* packages.
requiredPackageFiles: py.typed at the gpwcf package root to mark inline typing information.
packageData: Include only runtime files explicitly required by shipped package modules.
Do not include .docs, .poc, .dependencies, .env, PoC evidence, consumer Stage Models, Generator data, or local virtual-environment assets in the wheel.
packageDiscovery.tests: Tests remain repository verification assets and are not imported as runtime package modules. Their inclusion in sdist is a separate source-distribution convenience decision; they are never part of the installed runtime package.

installationCommands.guarantee: Installs the optional Prefect runtime dependency while preserving the separate Integration import boundary.
Editable integration development with explicit optional runtime.

lockStrategy.metadataVsLock: pyproject.toml declares direct runtime requirements. Lock files pin the complete resolved environment for reproducible developer/CI/deployment profiles.

prefectLock.purpose: Record the minimized exact Prefect 3.9.2 transitive runtime closure with hashes/platform markers after clean isolated resolution.
prefectLock.creationGate: Must be reconstructed from a clean environment that installs only gpwcf[prefect], then reviewed for runtime relevance, licenses, markers, and hashes.
prefectLock.notAllowed: Do not copy the 106-package Prefect environment snapshot as the minimal lock.

buildLock.purpose: Pin the build frontend and any developer tools required to create/verify sdist and wheel.
buildLock.runtimeUse: Never installed as a consumer runtime dependency.

developmentLock.purpose: Pin selected test/type-check/lint/architecture-validation tools once the project's verification toolchain is explicitly approved.
developmentLock.currentStatus: No GPWCF-specific third-party test/type-check/lint dependency is currently declared. Do not populate speculative tools before the test policy is selected.

lockStrategy.solutionAggregator: The SMRB root requirements.txt remains the solution-level developer aggregator. It is not replaced by package metadata and must not silently add the Prefect extra to every Core consumer profile.

dependencyEnvironmentIsolation.rule: Continue using the existing SMRB shared dependency ownership and environment. Do not create GPWCF/.dependencies, copy the shared environment, or assume the contents of .dependencies are shipped package dependencies.
dependencyEnvironmentIsolation.packageRule: The installed distribution is resolved from pyproject metadata and the selected extra, not from the developer's currently activated .env.

buildOutputs.sourceOfTruth: The source package under src/gpwcf and pyproject.toml.
buildOutputs.repositoryPolicy: Generated build outputs are not committed unless a separate repository release policy explicitly requires them.

coreOnlyCleanEnvironment: Create a clean CPython 3.15.1 x64 environment with no Prefect and no Generator dependencies.
Install the built wheel using pip install gpwcf.
Verify Prefect is not installed and no Prefect module was imported.
Verify no pygccxml or Generator module is imported/required.
Verify optional Supporting Pattern submodules can be omitted.
prefectExtraCleanEnvironment: Create a clean CPython 3.15.1 x64 environment.
Install gpwcf[prefect] from the built artifact using the minimized lock.
Verify Core remains independently importable and does not import private Integration modules.
Run a minimal Stage/Step/SPU binding smoke test against the accepted native topology.
metadataInspection: Inspect wheel METADATA and verify no unconditional Requires-Dist: prefect entry exists.
Verify prefect==3.9.2 is guarded by the prefect extra marker.
Verify no pygccxml, Generator, C++/vcpkg, or SMRB development dependencies appear in GPWCF metadata.
Verify package metadata declares the supported Python range.
artifactConsistency: Build both wheel and sdist in an isolated build environment.
Install from wheel and from sdist into clean Core-only environments.
Verify both artifacts contain the same supported public package modules.
Verify .docs, .poc, .dependencies, .env, and consumer assets are excluded from the wheel.
importIsolation: Import gpwcf.public_api.core in an environment without Prefect.
Inspect sys.modules/import tracing to prove Prefect is not imported transitively.
Import only one optional Supporting Pattern and verify other patterns are not loaded.
Import gpwcf.public_api.integrations.prefect only in the Prefect-extra environment.

changes: Keep pyproject.toml as required project/build metadata.
Record setuptools.build_meta and the pinned build-system requirement.
Record the single gpwcf distribution with optional Prefect extra.
Add py.typed and package discovery configuration.
Add proposed lock files as dependency manifests only; do not create a dependency bundle.
Resolve the distribution arrangement as one distribution plus optional Prefect extra for the initial release.
Record setuptools==84.2.1 as build-only and prefect==3.9.2 as optional runtime.
Retain Prefect transitive closure as a release gate.
Separate build/dev/test locks from runtime requirements.

externalTechnicalReferences.supports: Setuptools 84.2.1 release metadata and declared Python >=3.10 requirement.
setuptools.build_meta PEP 517 backend and wheel/sdist build hooks.
Python 3.15 build support in the Setuptools 84.x release line.

externalTechnicalReferences.source: Python Packaging User Guide: Writing pyproject.toml
externalTechnicalReferences.supports: PEP 517/518 build-system declaration and PEP 621 project metadata.

conformanceRequirements.requirement: The initial release uses one gpwcf distribution with a rigorously optional Prefect extra.
Core base runtime dependencies remain empty.
Prefect is declared only under the prefect optional extra as prefect==3.9.2.
The package uses src/gpwcf layout and PEP 621 metadata in pyproject.toml.
The build backend is setuptools.build_meta pinned to setuptools==84.2.1, subject to clean CPython 3.15.1 build verification.
Build-system dependencies are isolated from runtime dependencies.
The wheel includes py.typed and excludes docs, PoC, dependencies, virtual environment, and consumer-specific assets.
Core-only installation/import succeeds without Prefect, pygccxml, or Generator assets.
The Prefect extra installs Prefect 3.9.2 and its minimized verified transitive closure.
The 106-package environment snapshot is not used as the minimal Prefect dependency lock.
No GPWCF-local .dependencies directory or copied .env is created.
Build, development, test, and verification tools are excluded from runtime metadata.
A future split distribution requires an explicit release/dependency rationale and compatibility policy.

acceptanceCriteria: One distribution and the optional Prefect extra preserve the Core-only dependency/import guarantee.
Prefect 3.9.2 remains opt-in and is not a base dependency.
Setuptools build backend and Python 3.15.1 compatibility have a documented evidence basis and clean-build gate.
Project metadata, package discovery, py.typed, and source layout are explicit.
Prefect transitive dependency lock is minimized and reproducible before release.
SMRB shared dependency assets remain shared development state and are not copied into GPWCF.
Wheel/sdist and import-isolation verification profiles are defined.
No actual pyproject.toml, lock file, package source, or environment is modified by this artifact.

changeControl.authority: Wave 6 packaging proposal. It becomes an implementation constraint only after review and explicit acceptance.
changeControl.sourceContractPolicy: This artifact does not create or modify pyproject.toml, requirements files, lock files, or source packages.
changeControl.implementationGate: Create the actual pyproject.toml only after all Wave 6 artifacts and governing-artifact reconciliation are accepted.
changeControl.nextStep: Design 16.00_Public_API_Architecture.json with exact stable import namespaces, exported contract groups, consumer extension points, optional imports, and versioning rules.
